title: POV day
premise: First person, one continuous thread through a day. The camera is your eyes and never cuts away to look at you.

copy.hook: POV: the day nobody posts about
copy.cta: Follow if this is your year too

shots.what: Eyes-open moment — a ceiling, an alarm, a door from the inside
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Hold the camera where your head would be, at your eye height, and keep it there for the entire reel. The moment it drops to chest height the illusion goes.

shots.what: Your hands doing the first thing of the day
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Hands entering from the bottom of the frame, not the sides. That is what separates POV from a close-up.

shots.what: Going out — a door, stairs, a street from walking height
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Walk smoothly, roll your feet. Gimbal if you have it; without one, keep your elbows locked to your ribs.

shots.what: The main thing the day is about, from inside it
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Look at what you are doing, not at the camera. Whatever your hands are on should be the centre of the frame.

shots.what: A detail from the same viewpoint — a screen, a tool, food
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: The one place you may break eye height, briefly, to look down at something.

shots.what: What the day was for — the view, the finish, the sit-down
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Lift your eyeline into it rather than cutting to it — a POV reel pays off by looking up.

shots.what: Stillness. Hands at rest, a drink, the light going.
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Brace the camera and do not move for eight seconds. The whole reel has been moving; this is where it stops.

shots.what: The last thing you look at before it ends
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Still, simple, uncluttered centre. Hold five seconds.
